primary_claim: In Public Goods Game simulations, traditional LLMs like Llama-3.3-70B maintain ~90% contribution rates and largely choose costly sanctioning institutions, while reasoning-focused models (o1, o3-mini series) contribute only ~40% on average, more readily adopt the free-rider Nash-equilibrium strategy, and rarely opt into sanctioning institutions.

effect.metric: average token contribution in Public Goods Game
effect.value: traditional LLMs (e.g. Llama-3.3-70B) average ~18.7/20 tokens (~90%) vs reasoning models (e.g. o1-mini) average ~5.4/20 tokens (~27%); summary states ~90% vs ~40% contribution overall

contradicts_or_qualifies: challenges the assumption that enhancing an AI's general reasoning capabilities will naturally improve its performance across all domains, particularly in cooperative social settings
stated_future_work: focus on training paradigms that explicitly foster pro-social reasoning, potentially leveraging specialized architectures aimed at improving cooperation
quote: Traditional language models, like Llama-3.3-70B, contribute over 90% of their resources and maintain stable cooperation.
